node.date_label: The Sinews of Power (1989) · Consumption and the World of Goods (coeditor Roy Porter) (1993) · The Pleasures of the Imagination (1997)
node.description: Historian of eighteenth-century Britain whose work crosses state finance, cultural production and consumption. In his2026 memoir Brewer explains that The Sinews of Power challenged the idea of a weak British state while investigating resistance and special interests within fiscal expansion. He resists fixed disciplinary labels and treats literature and the arts as connected historical practices rather than autonomous masterpieces.

proposed_edges.relationship: The Sinews of Power makes taxation, administration and the financing of war central to the eighteenth-century British state.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Brewer’s own2026 research retrospective also emphasizes resistance and policy-shaping by interests; strong state does not mean unlimited state.

proposed_edges.relationship: The Pleasures of the Imagination examines cultural making and reception across arts and provincial settings.
